scenes.headline: How VisionSIM turns one render into many sensors
scenes.sub: Event, single-photon, time-of-flight and thermal, from one Blender scene.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bolo! Simulators give you perfect pictures. Real sensors never do. Here is how VisionSIM closes that gap.

scenes.text: Render the scene once with exact ground truth, then replay those clean frames through a physical model of each sensor, failure modes included.
scenes.mark: a physical model of each sensor
scenes.say: Render once, with exact labels. Then replay the clean frames through a physical model of each sensor, failures and all.

steps.say: Blender renders the scene once, with depth, flow and normals for every frame.
Fast sensors need thousands of frames a second, so a video interpolator fills the gaps.
Then each sensor model reads the same clean frames. Change a threshold, and nothing is rendered again.
Thermal is different. The renderer's own light becomes heat, and a solver spreads it.

items.say: smoothed by a filter that is slow in the dark.
Every time the change crosses its threshold, it fires an event.
Then it waits. In this code, a missed crossing is delayed, not lost.

scenes.label: events from one four-stop lamp switch on 9,216 pixels
scenes.note: about 14 per pixel, in my port of the emulator
scenes.say: Switch a lamp on, and every pixel fires at once: over a hundred and thirty thousand events.

parts.note: chance the pixel sees at least one photon
parts.say: A single-photon pixel records one bit: did a photon arrive?

parts.note: Poisson arrivals, counted at most once
parts.say: Arrivals are random, so the chance is one minus e to the minus flux. Average many bits, and invert.

scenes.title: Flux error after summing bits
scenes.note: median error at one photon per frame
scenes.say: At one photon per frame, five hundred and twelve bits get within about four percent.

steps.say: Hot tea goes into one cup made of ceramic, steel and aluminium.
Seconds later the aluminium glows first. It spreads heat far faster than ceramic.

scenes.text: Synchronised, perfectly labelled sensors come free when the sensors are equations; the parameters decide whether they tell the truth.
scenes.say: When sensors are equations, sync and labels are free. The parameters decide whether they tell the truth.
Render once. Emulate every sensor. And check what the code really ships.
